samples.summary: The fix only reorders the AGENT's work; the fix job's own post-push steps still lose the same race, so the stated outcome ("work done after the push is not reliably delivered") is only half addressed
samples.evidence: The change is entirely prompt prose + a prompt-ordering test. But the `fix` job continues after the fixer step with "Upload fix execution log" (1776), "Write fix session job summary" (1787), "Page if the fix produced no commit" (1806), "Update loop status (fix outcome)" (1843) and "Record agent effort metrics" (1868) — all of which execute AFTER the fixer's push and therefore inside the same ~30s cancellation window the diff documents (34s/34s/31s on #757). By the doc's own measurement those steps lose two rounds out of three: loop-status never records `fix-pushed`, metrics for the review-fix session are never recorded, and the no-commit page check may never run. Neither the prompt change nor docs/design/harness-engineering.md's new section acknowledges this, even though it is the same defect at the same site; the doc frames ordering as the whole fix ("the fix is ordering rather than machinery"). Machinery-level options (e.g. a job/step not subject to the workflow concurrency group, or posting metrics/loop-status before the fixer's push) are not considered.
searchedFor: read .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml lines 1580-1915 (all steps after the fixer)
docs/design/harness-engineering.md new section text in the diff

samples.summary: The design doc's survey of other agent workflows exempts agent-fix.yml but never mentions agent-iterate-ci.yml, whose prompt still puts its report AFTER the push
samples.evidence: The new doc section explicitly clears `.github/workflows/agent-fix.yml` ("declares no workflow-level concurrency") but says nothing about agent-iterate-ci.yml, which has the same shape: it pushes (lines 348-370) and only THEN says "Then reply in the PR's verification thread noting what you fixed" (line 372). Its job-level concurrency is `cancel-in-progress: true` (line 85), so a re-triggered CI-fix run can cancel the in-flight one and lose that reply. Either the exposure is real and unfixed, or the survey should say why it is not, the way it does for agent-fix.yml.

samples.summary: A workflow-prompt-prose assertion is filed in fix-report's unit test file, coupling an unrelated module's suite to the panel YAML's wording
samples.evidence: The new test reads .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml and asserts on prose markers (`BEFORE PUSHING`, `PUSH LAST`) inside fix-report.test.mjs, which otherwise tests scripts/agent/fix-report.mjs. There is precedent for workflow-reading tests (scripts/agent/loop-status.test.mjs:390), so this is a placement/taste call rather than a rule violation, but the assertion is about the panel prompt, not about fix-report, and the literal-string coupling (`Push with \`git push --no-verify\``, `rebuttal.mjs post`) means a harmless prompt rewording reds an unrelated suite.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts the fix job's post-push steps lose the cancellation race and that no machinery guards them. Every step it names is already gated `if: always() && steps.guard.outputs.proceed == 'true'` (agent-review-panel.yml:1777, 1788, 1844, 1869), and `always()` runs on a cancelled run — a fact this repo documents from its own observation ("Under `always()` this step still ran" at :816-819; "a panel the concurrency guard CANCELLED, whose `always()` verdict step still wrote six fail-closed reds" at harness-engineering.md:1231). So loop-status `fix-pushed` and the review-fix metrics record are delivered on a cancelled fix job, contradicting the finding's premise. The single non-`always()` step, "Page if the fix produced no commit" (:1806), is deliberately skipped on cancellation and correctly so: cancellation implies a push advanced the head, which is exactly the branch where that step pages nothing (:1821-1822). Loop-status is further designed to self-heal a missed update (:1040-1041). The claim that machinery-level cancellation options were "not considered" is also refuted at the same site: `close-stuck-checks` was split out of `stalled` specifically so cleanup runs on cancelled runs while paging does not (:1898-1923 vs :1980-1993), with the reasoning recorded in harness-engineering.md:1316-1323.
